Pure Mg (99.9 %), Mg-30Gd, Mg-25Y, Mg-30Zr (wt%) master alloy and pure Zn were melted in an electric resistance furnace at 730 – 750 ◦ C protected by a mixed atmosphere of CO2 and SF6 with the volumetric ratio of 99:1, and the melt was poured into the cooling crystallizer at 710 – 720 ◦ C to prepare the billet with a diameter of 90 mm.
Subsequently, homogenization treatment was performed at 520 ◦ C for 12 h in a vacuum heat treatment furnace, followed by rapid quenching in a heated water of ~90 º C.
Prior to extrusion, homogenized billets underwent preheating at 510 ◦ C for 1 h, while the extrusion dies were preheated at 350 ◦ C for 1 h.

The backward extrusion process was conducted at 350 ◦ C with an extrusion ratio of ~5:1 and a controlled ram speed of 0.1 mm/s. Post extrusion, the 30 mm diameter of extrusion bars were immediately water-quenched to ambient temperature to inhibit grain coarsening.
